The Cameron graph is a [[strongly regular graph]] of parameters <math>(231, 30, 9, 3)</math>. This means that it has 231 vertices, 30 edges per vertex, 9 triangles per edges, and 3 two-edge paths between every two non-adjacent vertices.<ref name=brouwer>{{citation
 | last = Brouwer | first = A. E.
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01788073
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Graphs and Combinatorics
 | mr = 1117128
 | pages = 21–29
 | title = Uniqueness and nonexistence of some graphs related to {{math|''M''<sub>22</sub>}}
 | url = https://www.win.tue.nl/~aeb/preprints/6366A.pdf
 | volume = 2
 | year = 1986}}</ref>

It can be obtained from a [[Steiner system]] <math>S(3,6,22)</math> (a collection of 22 elements and 6-element blocks with each triple of elements covered by exactly one block). In this construction, the 231 vertices of the graph correspond to the 231 [[unordered pair]]s of elements. Two vertices are adjacent whenever they come from two disjoint pairs whose union belongs to one of the blocks.<ref name=brouwer/>

It is one of a small number of strongly regular graphs on which the [[Mathieu group M22|Mathieu group {{math|''M''<sub>22</sub>}}]] acts as symmetries taking [[vertex-transitive graph|every vertex to every other vertex]]. The smaller [[M22 graph|{{math|''M''<sub>22</sub>}} graph]] is another.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Crnković | first1 = Dean
 | last2 = Mostarac | first2 = Nina
 | last3 = Švob | first3 = Andrea
 | arxiv = 2101.02790
 | title = Distance-regular graphs obtained from the Mathieu groups
 | year = 2021}}</ref>
